probe: bar-parity of the HH^1 outer class acting on the cocenter
description: Reads the bar-parity of the induced action of the HH^1 outer derivation class on the cocenter HH_0 = A/[A,A]. The action is class-canonical because inner derivations induce zero on HH_0 (asserted). Bar-EVEN kills the fibre-level c_3 carrier route to the same bar-parity invariant that closed the real Gram-resolvent route; bar-ODD would clear that obstruction.
method: exact cyclotomic linear algebra; Der = nullspace of Leibniz constraints, Inn = span of ad_x, cocenter by complementary coordinates; bar applied SEMILINEARLY (Delta^bar = M bar(Delta) bar(M)). No fit.

assertions.name: root_of_unity_points_valid
assertions.detail: q=i has [2]_q=0, q=zeta_6 has [3]_q=0; both on the unit circle with conjugate(z) = z^{-1}, so the bar branch is valid

assertions.name: inner_acts_as_zero_on_cocenter[q = i        ([2]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: every ad_x induces the zero map on HH_0, so the induced action depends only on the HH^1 class (test is canonical)

assertions.name: bar_is_involutive[q = i        ([2]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: BAR_A * bar(BAR_A) = I on A (semilinear involution verified)

assertions.name: bar_involutive_on_cocenter[q = i        ([2]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: Mbar * bar(Mbar) = I on HH_0 (guards the semilinear branch)

assertions.name: lambda_has_norm_one[q = i        ([2]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: lambda*bar(lambda) = 1 -- the Hilbert-90 hypothesis for Q(zeta)/Q(zeta)^+, so lambda = bar(c)/c is solvable and the parity is a choice of normalization, not an invariant

assertions.name: delta_is_class_canonical[q = i        ([2]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: 6 alternative representatives (outer + ad_x for each basis x) all reproduce Delta exactly

assertions.name: inner_acts_as_zero_on_cocenter[q = zeta_6   ([3]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: every ad_x induces the zero map on HH_0, so the induced action depends only on the HH^1 class (test is canonical)

assertions.name: bar_is_involutive[q = zeta_6   ([3]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: BAR_A * bar(BAR_A) = I on A (semilinear involution verified)

assertions.name: bar_involutive_on_cocenter[q = zeta_6   ([3]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: Mbar * bar(Mbar) = I on HH_0 (guards the semilinear branch)

assertions.name: lambda_has_norm_one[q = zeta_6   ([3]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: lambda*bar(lambda) = 1 -- the Hilbert-90 hypothesis for Q(zeta)/Q(zeta)^+, so lambda = bar(c)/c is solvable and the parity is a choice of normalization, not an invariant

assertions.name: delta_is_class_canonical[q = zeta_6   ([3]_q = 0)]
assertions.detail: 6 alternative representatives (outer + ad_x for each basis x) all reproduce Delta exactly

assertions.name: inner_acts_as_zero_on_cocenter[q = 2        (semisimple control)]
assertions.detail: every ad_x induces the zero map on HH_0, so the induced action depends only on the HH^1 class (test is canonical)

assertions.name: bar_is_involutive[q = 2        (semisimple control)]
assertions.detail: BAR_A * bar(BAR_A) = I on A (semilinear involution verified)

verdict: THE PROPOSED PRUNE DOES NOT EXIST. The bar-parity of the HH^1 outer class acting on HH_0 is NOT an invariant of the class: it is a choice of normalization. Delta^bar is proportional to Delta at both root-of-unity points (lambda = +1 at q=i, lambda = -1 at q=zeta_6), and lambda*bar(lambda) = 1 -- the Hilbert-90 hypothesis for Q(zeta)/Q(zeta)^+ -- so lambda = bar(c)/c is always solvable. Demonstrated constructively rather than argued: rescaling the representative by a bar-ODD scalar FLIPS the parity at both points (bar-EVEN -> bar-ODD at q=i; bar-ODD -> bar-EVEN at q=zeta_6). CONSEQUENCE: bar-parity cannot prune the fibre-level c_3 carrier the way it pruned the real Gram resolvent. The route is NOT killed -- and NOT confirmed either. A finer invariant, or a construction that PINS the normalization, is required.
scope: scope-(a). This is a negative result about the TEST, not about the route: it shows the bar-parity readout carries no information for an un-normalized class. It does NOT exclude the HH^1 carrier. n=3 is the MECHANISM check: its non-semisimple points are [2]_q=0 and [3]_q=0, NOT the Bring [5]. The Bring fibre is H_5 at a 5th root of unity (bean qou-jcmw). The normalization-dependence argument is field-theoretic (Hilbert 90 over Q(zeta)/Q(zeta)^+) and does not depend on n, so it is expected to carry to H_5 -- which is why the expensive dim-120 H_5 parity computation should NOT be run expecting a prune.
why_the_real_route_pruned_but_this_does_: The real Gram resolvent lived over R, where bar acts trivially, so its parity was rigid and the bar-odd target S was genuinely unreachable. At a root of unity bar acts as the nontrivial Galois map zeta -> zeta^{-1}, and Q(zeta) CONTAINS bar-odd scalars (e.g. zeta - zeta^{-1}), so both parities are always available. That is precisely why the fibre-level route survived the real-route exclusion chain in the first place.
